For x $\in$ (0, 3/2), let f(x) = $\sqrt{x}$ , g(x) = tan x and h(x) = $\frac{1-x^{2}}{1+x^{2}}$. If $𝜙$ (x) =  ((hof)og)(x),  then $𝜙\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )$
 is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$𝜙(x)=((hof)og)(x)=h\left (\sqrt{\tan x}\right )$

$\Rightarrow 𝜙(x)=\frac{1-\tan x}{1+\tan x}=\tan \left (\frac{π}{4}-x\right )$

$\therefore$ $𝜙\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=\tan \left (\frac{π}{4}-\frac{π}{3}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \tan \left (-\frac{π}{12}\right )=\tan \frac{11π}{12}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text: If $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{\cot x}{\cot x+\cos ecx}dx$ = m($π$ + n), then m.n is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

text:
If $α$ and $β$ are the roots of the equation $375x^{2}$
– 25x – 2 = 0, then $\lim _{n\to \infty }\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}α^{r}+\lim _{n\to \infty }\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}β^{r}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $375x^{2}-25x-2=0$:

$α+β=\dfrac{25}{375}=\dfrac{1}{15},αβ=-\dfrac{2}{375}$

The roots are $\dfrac{25\pm \sqrt{3625}}{750}$, approximately $0.114$ and $-0.047$, so $|α|<1$ and $|β|<1$ and both geometric series converge:

$\dfrac{α}{1-α}+\dfrac{β}{1-β}=\dfrac{(α+β)-2αβ}{1-(α+β)+αβ}$

The numerator is $\dfrac{1}{15}+\dfrac{4}{375}=\dfrac{29}{375}$ and the denominator is $1-\dfrac{25}{375}-\dfrac{2}{375}=\dfrac{348}{375}$.

$\text{Sum}=\dfrac{29}{348}=\dfrac{1}{12}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
If $e^{y}$
 + xy = e, the ordered pair $\left (\frac{dy}{dx},\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\right )$ at x = 0 is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
y = 1 $\Rightarrow$ x = 0

$e^{y}\frac{dy}{dx}+x\frac{dy}{dx}+y=0$

$\Rightarrow e\frac{dy}{dx}+1=0\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{1}{e}$

$\Rightarrow e^{y}\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}+e^{y}\left (\frac{dy}{dx}\right )^{2}+x\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}+2\frac{dy}{dx}=0$

x = 0, y = 1

$\Rightarrow e\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}+e\left (-\frac{1}{e}\right )^{2}+0+2\left (-\frac{1}{e}\right )=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=\frac{1}{e^{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
If m is the minimum value of k for which the function f(x) = x$\sqrt{kx-x^{2}}$ is increasing in the interval [0,3]
and M is the maximum value of f in [0, 3] when k = m, then the ordered pair (m, M) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=x\sqrt{kx-x^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $f^{'}(x)=\sqrt{kx-x^{2}}+\frac{(k-2x)x}{2\sqrt{kx-x^{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2\left (kx-x^{2}\right )+kx-2x^{2}}{2\sqrt{kx-x^{2}}}=\frac{3kx-4x^{2}}{2\sqrt{kx-x^{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{x(3k-4x)}{2\sqrt{kx-x^{2}}}$

Now for increasing function

for f'(x) $\geq$ 0,   $\forall x\in [0,3]$

$\Rightarrow kx-x^{2}\geq 0,\forall x\in [0,3]andx(3k-4x)\geq 0,\forall x\in [0,3]$

$\Rightarrow x(x-k)\leq 0,\forall x\in [0,3]andx(4x-3k)\leq 0,\forall x\in [0,3]$

k $\geq$ 3 and k $\geq$ 4 $\Rightarrow$ k $\geq$ 4

$\Rightarrow$ m = 4

So f(x) is maximum when k = 4 then $3\sqrt{4\times 3-3^{2}}=3\sqrt{3}=M$

$\therefore$ (m, M) = (4, $3\sqrt{3}$)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
Consider the differential equation, $y^{2}dx+\left (x-\frac{1}{y}\right )dy=0$, If value of y is 1 when x = 1, then the value of x
for which y = 2, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$y^{2}dx+\left (x-\frac{1}{y}\right )dy=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dx}{dy}+\frac{x}{y^{2}}=\frac{1}{y^{3}}$

Integrating factor (I.F) = $e^{-\frac{1}{y}}$

Now x.$e^{-\frac{1}{y}}$ = $\int e^{-\frac{1}{y}}\frac{1}{y^{3}}dy$ by putting $-\frac{1}{y}$ = t

$x.e^{t} =$ $\int e^{t}(-t)dt$

$\Rightarrow xe^{t}=-(t.e^{t}-e^{t})+c$

$\Rightarrow xe^{-\frac{1}{y}}=e^{-\frac{1}{y}}\left (1+\frac{1}{y}\right )+c$

$\Rightarrow x=1+\frac{1}{y}+c.e^{\frac{1}{y}}$

It passes through (1, 1)

$\therefore$ c = $-\frac{1}{e}$

Equation of the curve is 

$x=1+\frac{1}{y}-e^{\frac{1}{y}-1}$
It passes through (k, 2)

$\therefore$ k = $1+\frac{1}{2}-e^{\frac{1}{2}-1}$
= $\frac{3}{2}$ - $\frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
If the area (in sq. units) of the region {(x, y) : $y^{2}$
$\leq$ 4x, x + y $\leq$ 1, x $\geq$ 0, y $\geq$ 0} is $a\sqrt{2}+b$, then a – b is equal
to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

Let P be the point common to x + y = 1 and $y^{2} = 4x$

Then $y^{2} = 4(1-y)$ $\Rightarrow$ $y^{2} + 4y - 4 = 0$ 

$\Rightarrow y=\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{16+16}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow y=-2+2\sqrt{2}$

Then P is (3 - $2\sqrt{2}$, -2 + $2\sqrt{2}$).

Hence shaded area = Area of region (OPN) + area of ($\Delta OPQ$)

$\Rightarrow \int\limits _{0}^{3-2\sqrt{2}}2\sqrt{xdx}+\frac{1}{2}\left [1-(3-2\sqrt{2})\right ]^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{3}2\left (\sqrt{2}-1\right )\left (3-2\sqrt{2}\right )+\frac{1}{2}\left [2(\sqrt{2}-1)\right ]^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{4}{3}\left \{-7+5\sqrt{2}\right \}+2\left (3-2\sqrt{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{20}{3}-4\right )\sqrt{2}+6-\frac{28}{3}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{8}{3}\sqrt{2}-\frac{10}{3}$

Then a = $\frac{8}{3}$ and b = $\frac{-10}{3}$, so a - b = 6
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
If A is a symmetric matrix and B is a skew-symmetric matrix such that A + B = $\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$, then AB is equal
to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A+B=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & -1 \end{array}\right ]=P(say)$

Now $A=\frac{P+P^{T}}{2}&B=\frac{P-P^{T}}{2}$

So $A=\frac{1}{2}\left (\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & -1 \end{array}\right ]+\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 \end{array}\right ]\right )=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 4 \\ 4 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$

$B=\frac{1}{2}\left (\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & -1 \end{array}\right ]-\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 \end{array}\right ]\right )=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$

So $AB=\left (\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 4 \\ 4 & -1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]\right )=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 4 & -2 \\ -1 & -4 \end{array}\right ]$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
Let $\vec{a}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-2\widehat{k}$ be two vectors. If a vector perpendicular to both the vectors
$\vec{a}+\vec{b}$ and $\vec{a}-\vec{b}$ has the magnitude 12 then one such vector is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Required vector is $\vec{r}$ = $λ\left (\left (a–+b–\right )\times \left (a–-b–\right )\right )$

$\Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ 4 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 \end{array}\right |=λ\left (16\hat{i}-16\hat{j}-8\widehat{k}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}=8λ\left (2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \left |\vec{r}\right |=|8λ|.3=12\Rightarrow 8λ=\pm 4$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}=\pm 4\left (2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}\right )$

text:
If $B=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 5 & 2α & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ α & 3 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$ is the inverse of a 3 × 3 matrix A, then the sum of all values of $α$ for which
det(A) + 1 = 0, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given |A| + 1 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ |A| = -1

$|B|=\left |A^{-1}\right |=\frac{1}{|A|}=-1$

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} 5 & 2α & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ α & 3 & -1 \end{array}\right |$ = -1

$\Rightarrow$ $5(-2-3)+2α(α)+1(-2α)=-1$

$\Rightarrow$ $2α^{2}-2α-24=0$

$\therefore$ sum of value of $α$ = $\frac{-(-2)}{2}=1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
A 2 m ladder leans against a vertical wall. If the top of the ladder begins to slide down the wall at the rate
25 cm/sec, then the rate (in cm/sec.) at which the bottom of the ladder slides away from the wall on the
horizontal ground when the top of the ladder is 1 m above the ground is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$x^{2} + y^{2} = 4$ $\Rightarrow$ $2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt}=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dx}{dt}=-\frac{y}{x}.\frac{dy}{dt}$

When upper end is 1m above the ground, $\frac{dx}{dt}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.(-25)=\frac{25}{\sqrt{3}}$ cm/sec.

text: Let f : R $\to$ R be a continuously differentiable function such that f(2) = 6 and f'(2) = $\frac{1}{48}$. If $\int\limits _{6}^{f(x)}4t^{3}dt$ = (x - 2)g(x), then $\lim _{x\to 2}g(x)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $\int\limits _{6}^{f(x)}4x^{3}dx=g(x).(x-2)$

$\Rightarrow g(x)=$ $\frac{\int\limits _{0}^{f(x)}4x^{3}dx}{x-2}$

$\therefore$ $\lim _{x\to 2}g(x)=\lim _{x\to 2}\frac{\int\limits _{0}^{f(x)}4x^{3}dx}{x-2}$

At x = 2 this limit is in $\frac{0}{0}$ form.

So we can use L'Hopital's rule. Use leibniz intgral rule to differentiate the integration.

$\Rightarrow \lim _{x\to 2}\frac{4f^{3}(x).f^{'}(x)}{1}=4\times 6^{3}\times \frac{1}{48}=18$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot
